title: Unsafe pointer dereference without bounds check
description: read_byte_unchecked uses raw pointer arithmetic (ptr.add(index)) without verifying index < data.len(). Callers like validate_printable_ascii pass an external len parameter that may exceed the slice bounds, causing undefined behavior.

title: unwrap() on user-supplied input parsing
description: parse_port calls .parse::<u16>().unwrap() on user-provided input. Non-numeric or out-of-range input will panic instead of returning a meaningful error.

title: Silent error context loss in From<ParseError> for AppError
description: The From<ParseError> impl discards the original error's kind, offset, and message, replacing them with a generic 'parse error' string. This makes debugging impossible since all parse errors look identical after conversion.

title: Buffer overread from unchecked payload length
description: next_frame reads payload_len from the wire (untrusted input) and indexes remaining[14..14+payload_len] without checking that 14+payload_len <= remaining.len(). A crafted message with a large payload_len causes a panic (in debug) or buffer overread. The max_payload_size field exists but is never consulted.

title: Panic in Drop impl via unwrap()
description: Connection's Drop impl calls write_ack().unwrap(). If write_ack ever returns Err (currently infallible but the signature says Result), this will panic during drop, which can abort the process during stack unwinding.
